full_judgment:
2. Material facts relevant for disposal of this Rule, briefly, are that the petitioner as plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 73 of 2006 in the Court of the learned Assistant Judge for specific performance of contract against the defendant opposite parties. Ultimately, the suit was decreed on contest by the judgment and decree dated 25-1-2016. Against which the defendant, Mst. Misti Begum filed Title Appeal No. 44 of 2016 before the learned District Judge, Narsingdi and thereafter, while the appeal was in progress the added opposite party Nos. 4 & 5 namely, Sheikh Delwar Hossain and Md Asaduzzaman Tipu filed an application under Order I, rule 10 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for addition of party stating, inter-alia, that they purchased the suit land within the full knowledge of the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 73 of 2006 and others by 2 registered deeds dated 6-9-2016 and on the same date the vendor handed over possession of the said land to them and since then they have been paying rent and taxes to the Government. The added opposite party Nos. 4-5 in the month of November, 2017 for the first time came to know that a suit being Civil Suit No. 73 of 2006 for specific performance of contract in respect of their land has been decreed in which they are in possession and against the said decree the plaintiffs preferred Title Appeal No. 44 of 2016, which is now pending before the learned District Judge, Narsingdi and in the attending facts and circumstances they have direct interest over the suit land and that they may be added as parties in the appeal for adequate disposal of the appeal. 

 5. Mr Biksh Kumar Paul, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-petitioners in the course of his argument takes me through the revisional application and other materials on record and then submits that admittedly, the plaintiff filed the suit for specific performance of contract and the learned Assistant Judge on due consideration of the entire materials on record factually found the plaintiff has succeeded to prove his case and accordingly decreed the suit and thereafter, the defendants preferred Title Appeal No. 44 of 2016 and while the appeal was in progress the stranger purchasers all on a sudden filed an application under Order I, rule 10 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for addition of parties stating that they purchased total 19.5 decimals of land out of which 18.5 decimals of land is related with the suit land and it is on record that the stranger purchasers are in no way connected or parties to the agreement of bainanama in question and the Court of appeal below without applying its judicial mind into the facts and circumstance of the case and law bearing on the subject most illegally allowed the applicants to be added as the respondent Nos. 4-5. Finally, the learned Advocate relying on the decisions reported in 43 DLR (AD) 107, 19 BLD (HC) 485, 24 BLD (AD) 47, 14 BLT (AD) 16, 58 DLR 62, 13 BLT (AD) 206, 9 BLC (AD) 114, 8 BLT (AD) 301 submits that since the added opposite parties purchased a part of the suit land during pendency of the suit and it is on record that they are not parties to the agreement in question and they cannot be made party in the appeal or suit and in this case there is no special circumstances in which the opposite parties can be added as parties to fortify their case although the Court of appeal below without applying its judicial mind into the facts and circumstances of the case mechanically allowed the prayer for addition of party, which resulted in the failure of justice.
